Introducing Colours

In colour theory, colours are divided into two main categories based on undertone:

Warm

All colours with a warm temperature.

Warm-toned colours have a yellow or golden base. People with warm undertones have yellow or golden undertones.

and

Cool

All colours with a cool temperature.

Cool-toned colours have a blue or pink base. People with cool undertones have blue or pink undertones.

From this warm and cool undertone concept, the 4 Season Colour Analysis is developed. Each season is categorized based on three key factors:

• Temperature (Warm vs. Cool) • Clarity (Bright vs. Muted) • Depth (Light vs. Deep)

SPRING

  • • Warm
  • • Bright
  • • Light

SUMMER

  • • Cool
  • • Muted
  • • Light

AUTUMN

  • • Warm
  • • Muted
  • • Deep

WINTER

  • • Cool
  • • Bright
  • • Deep

These factors determine which season a colour belongs to based on the natural undertones of an individual.

Concepts to Personal Colour Around the World

The evolution of colour harmony theory across centuries and continents:

Renaissance
Leonardo da Vinci's Colour Theory — Focus on harmony and contrast
17th Century
Newton's prism experiments — creation of the colour wheel
Early 19th
Goethe & Chevreul's principle of colour harmony
1920
Itten's seasonal colour — Caygill's Personal Color System
1980
Color Me Beautiful — Popularizes seasonal colour analysis in the West
1990s–2000s
East Asian systems introduce detailed tone-based analysis

The roots of Colour analysis method have been around since 1920 coined by Johannes Itten. Since then, experts have adapted methods to local beauty standards and created various colour systems.

4-Season Colour Analysis

1970s by Carole Jackson

Popular in the US, based on Johannes Itten's color theory. Divides individuals into Spring, Summer, Autumn, and Winter based on warm/cool and light/dark characteristics.

12-Season Colour Analysis

1980s by Suzanne Caygill & Sci \ ART

Popular worldwide, an extension of the 4-season system. Introduces subcategories like Light Spring, Soft Autumn, Cool Summer, and Bright Winter for more precise colour matching.

Japanese PCCS

1960s by Japan Color Research Institute

Developed in Japan, used in design, fashion, and beauty. Classifies colors into tonal families of 4 seasons with 3 sub-seasons each (Cool, Soft, Light, Warm, Deep, Muted, and Bright tones).

Korean Personal Colour Systems

2010s by Major Fashion-Beauty Experts

Introduces micro-tonal grading: Pale, Light, Clear Bright, Strong Vivid, Muted Soft, Dull, Middle, Deep, and Dark tones tailored for Asian skin depth.

Tonal Colour System

1990s by David Zyla

Popular in the UK, based on the Colour Theory of Albert Munsell. Uses 6 dominant colouring types: Light, Deep, Warm, Cool, Clear, and Soft.

In Korea alone, leading trending centers offer different methods — some even give different seasons for different parts of a client's body (hair, makeup, clothes) which can disrupt harmony.

These interpretations have deviated from the core principle of HARMONY and from achieving a lifetime result. Such techniques favor frequent visits, whereas Personal Colour should be a single lifetime investment based on your natural undertones that you are born with.

Color Analysis and what we believe in is about HARMONY.

Embracing our rich spectrum of skintone diversity in Indonesia, Colourist synthesizes the finest global methodologies from Japan, Korea, Hong Kong, Bangkok, and Australia to establish the highest benchmark that is most empowering and relevant for Indonesians.
